key_insight: Wat3R shows that underwater 3D geometry can be learned without expensive underwater annotations by adapting a model trained on air to the underwater domain. It uses semi-supervised cross-domain learning to make feed-forward 3D reconstruction practical in scenes where labeled data is scarce.
problem_solved: The paper addresses underwater 3D reconstruction, which is difficult because of light attenuation, scattering, and the lack of large-scale, high-quality 3D annotations.
method: Adapts feed-forward 3D reconstruction models from air images to underwater scenes using a cross-domain semi-supervised framework.
Removes the dependence on dense underwater 3D labels by leveraging unlabeled or weakly labeled data.
Learns robust geometry despite underwater visual degradation such as haze, color shift, and scattering.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it reduces the annotation burden for 3D learning in hard-to-collect environments. It can enable scalable underwater mapping, robotics, marine inspection, and scientific exploration with less manual labeling.

paper_title: Wat3R: Underwater 3D Geometry Learning without Annotations
paper_authors: Jiangwei Ren, Xingyu Jiang, Zijie Song, Wei Xu, Hongkai Lin
